> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a6a4d3e9c777116708486b48e0fc985cd788667` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9173b6cb975ff32c0ebc76d1e27ec90e7bf9e0eb` — the merge of head `20a5c41cfb130c7a36778b85f8d5701af92c63c6` into base `6a6a4d3e9c777116708486b48e0fc985cd788667`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9173b6cb975ff32c0ebc76d1e27ec90e7bf9e0eb && git checkout 9173b6cb975ff32c0ebc76d1e27ec90e7bf9e0eb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6a6a4d3e9c777116708486b48e0fc985cd788667 20a5c41cfb130c7a36778b85f8d5701af92c63c6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6a6a4d3e9c777116708486b48e0fc985cd788667 && git merge --no-ff 20a5c41cfb130c7a36778b85f8d5701af92c63c6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a6a4d3e9c777116708486b48e0fc985cd788667
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6a6a4d3e9c777116708486b48e0fc985cd788667` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `20a5c41cfb130c7a36778b85f8d5701af92c63c6`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read, and nothing else: card #23027 (body; triage 6122964017; claim 6123839199; report 6125201870; seat answer and claim amendment 6125260474; report 6127009648), PR #23045 (body, the 8-file list, the net diff against `main` from merge base `df7a137923`), and the 47 check-runs on this head. Every required context reads `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`); `Check Changeset` and `Check PR Size` read `success`; no governed path is in the file list. The at-rest texts cited below were read on `origin/main` `ec7f7f83b6`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The second root, `packages[i].manifest` — right.** `applyArtifactForwardConversions` now runs ONE `replay` closure — the same `applyConversions` call, the same `includeRetired: true`, the same `excludeConversionIds` decided once above it — over the definition and then over each body (`replayPackageBodies`). No second entry list exists in the diff, which is what triage directed. The spec already reads a body this way: `migrations/chain.ts` (`stackDeclaresVerdict`) treats `packages[].manifest` as a collection carrier, and the one registry entry that reads a manifest (`manifest-permissions-string-list-removed`) already walks `packages[i].manifest` from the root, so a body run as a root finds no `manifest` key to strip twice. Copy-on-write holds at both levels and is pinned (an untouched body and the artifact's own manifest keep their references; a definition with nothing to convert comes back as itself). A `packages` that is not an array, an entry or a body that is not an object come back as given, and `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` stays the refusal — right, the conversion never gates. All 66 retired step-18 entries are pinned over a body in both directions, which is the structural check that no entry misreads a body's manifest fields as a collection.
2. **The window is the artifact's, decided once — right.** ADR-0087's 2026-09-13 addendum reads "a compiled artifact inside the versioned window its own manifest opens": the subject is the compiled artifact, and an artifact has one manifest. `composeStacks(…, { manifest: 'preserve' })` documents that the singular `manifest` "is retained, not replaced … so the artifact keeps an artifact-level identity (ADR-0130 D6 — one artifact, one version)"; ADR-0130 D4 says forward compatibility "rides on `manifest.engines.protocol`" (singular), and D1 that everything inside one artifact is delivered atomically by one publisher. The boot handshake judges that same manifest and no other: `assertArtifactProtocolCompatible` reads `bundle.manifest ?? bundle`, `AppPlugin.init` reads `this.bundle.manifest || this.bundle`, and `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` parses each entry against `ArtifactPackageSchema` without comparing a body's range to the runtime. A per-body window would let the package listed first decide whether the artifact boots after the handshake had already answered from the package listed last. The floor stands in for when the artifact was built, and one `os build` writes every body. Both directions are pinned in metadata-core ("a body's own `engines.protocol` is not read, in either direction"). Residual, named not failed: under `'preserve'` the top-level manifest is whichever input stack came last, so the window follows that package's authored range — the same arbitrariness the handshake already carries, and not this PR's to change.
3. **`Clause-②: no` — holds.** (a) Public surface: `convertArtifactAtLoad` is declared in `packages/runtime/src/load-artifact-bundle.ts`; `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` is not in the diff, and its line 215 re-exports only `loadArtifactBundle, mergeRuntimeModule, isHttpUrl, readArtifactSource`; `packages/runtime/package.json` `exports` has the one entry `.` (`dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`), and `files` is `dist` plus two docs. The function is unreachable from the package's exports — a module export only, as the body says. `ArtifactForwardConversionVerdict`, `ArtifactForwardConversionOptions` and `ArtifactConversionNotice` are unchanged in the diff (one doc comment on `path`). (b) Accept set: the window, the entry list and the default-flip exclusions are unchanged; nothing authored past the window is newly admitted — WINDOW SHUT is pinned at all three layers (metadata-core, the metadata door, and the runtime door as `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGE_ENTRY`/422 naming `packages[0]`). The option-B artifacts that now boot were inside the accept set ADR-0087 declares for data at rest and were refused by a defect of reach; a runtime starting to deliver a declared behaviour is the reading triage applied to this lane's #22957, and it holds here. Not a widening.
4. **Two disk reads, one funnel — right.** On `origin/main` the boot path reads the artifact file in exactly two places under `packages/runtime/src`: `load-artifact-bundle.ts` (`readArtifactSource`) and `resolve-project-database.ts:239` (`readConfigDeclaredDefault`); `default-host.ts` imports only `isHttpUrl` and reads nothing. Both now call `convertArtifactAtLoad`, which is one call of `applyArtifactForwardConversions` — the same function `MetadataPlugin._convertArtifactForward` runs on the raw file through `artifactSource.path`. One implementation, one policy, three readers; idempotence is pinned once (a second conversion of the loader's output is the same reference with no notices), so the door prints its one summary and nothing is converted twice. Not a second opinion. Routing the resolver is load-bearing: without it the resolver's own strict read refused the body and DECLINED, booting against the unified default database — a silent wrong-database boot in place of a loud refusal, the direction AGENTS.md's "prefer failing to falling back" forbids; the dev's ablation leg and the resolver pin both show it.
5. **Order inside `loadArtifactBundle` — right.** The conversion runs after the envelope unwrap and the `grantedPermissions` carry-over, before the remote `runtimeModule` strip and before `mergeRuntimeModule`, which itself parses bodies strictly through `resolveArtifactCollections`. `mergeRuntimeModule` mutates the converted copy, and every caller uses the return value.
6. **Notice location — right.** `locateUnder` prefixes `path` and rewrites the one quoted path in `message`; the spelling it replaces (` at ${path}: `) is exactly what `conversions/apply.ts` writes, and the metadata-core test asserts the rewritten message.
7. **`app-plugin.ts` — comment only.** The diff is one comment block; the `servicePayload` logic is byte-unchanged. The new sentence is also the one residual worth naming: a `packages[]` bundle handed to `AppPlugin` by a route other than `loadArtifactBundle` still reaches the `manifest` service with unconverted bodies. No public door measured on the card reaches that route; it stays a note.
8. **Config boot (`composeStacks`) — answered.** Triage asked for it; the dev measured it refused at `defineStack` with the tombstone prescription. That is the authoring funnel teaching a live author, which ADR-0087 keeps distinct from data at rest. No fix owed.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23027-package-body-conversion.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/metadata-core` and `@objectstack/runtime` — **right**. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3: a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`; `pr-automation.yml` "WHICH LEVEL": `minor` is owed for "a new exported symbol on an `index`, a new accepted key or value", and this diff adds neither (judgment ①3). The changeset body carries `Clause-②: no` on its own line, where `check-adr-0087-registration` reads it; no breaking declaration, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `Check Changeset` reads `success` on this head.
- PR line 2 `Clause-②: no`, no arm — **right**: neither a widening (no new export, no new accepted shape) nor a narrowing (nothing accepted before is refused now). The claim's own trigger for `yes` ("if the dev adds an exported member — a new verdict or option") did not fire.
- Line 1 `Fixes #23027` — right now that the measured door boots; the check-run "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" reads `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Report 6125201870 `open_questions` (who carries the runtime half; A, B or C) — **answered** by the seat in 6125260474 (A, on this PR; C refused), carried in this head; `open_questions` is empty in 6127009648.
- Deviation: `resolve-project-database.ts` is outside the amended surface — **accepted**: it is a reader that reads the file by another path, routed through the same single function, with the measured reason (the silent wrong-database boot) and its own ablation leg. The claim's "stop on a breach and explain it" was honoured in the report.
- `detectUnboundFormViewPredicateRoots` reads only top-level `views`, so an option-B body's form predicates get no boot notice — stays an **Acceptance note**: read, not measured at a door; a different mechanism from the conversion; the seat files it on a measurement.
- `pnpm lint` not run locally — `Lint · ESLint` reads `success` on this head. The earlier CI red (TS2345 in the new test at `6a01653b53`) is fixed in this head; `TypeScript Type Check` and `Type Check · workspace` read `success`.
- 909 changed lines, under the 3,000 human-merge line; no governed surface; nothing under `content/docs/releases/`.
- Observation for the seat, not a condition: the new runtime door test boots four real kernels, and AGENTS.md makes a test file over 10 s of wall its lane's card. No wall reading is in the report; `Test Core` is green on this head.
